Amy — really appreciate the candid note. We’ve been exploring structures that balance customer cashflow with price certainty; I sketched a proposal below that might match CloudNova’s requirements without a full prepay. High level: an escrowed advance-credit account + anchor-rate guarantee.

Proposal (summary):
- Term: 3 years (option to step down to 2 years)
- Advance-credit escrow: customer deposits an agreed amount (e.g., 40% of year 1 committed value) into a restricted credit account we hold; credits are drawn monthly to pay bills.
- Anchor-rate: while credits remain in escrow, the unit token rate for your primary model is fixed (price anchor) at the agreed rate — protects you from increases.
- Ramp protection: if usage grows >25% YoY, subsequent years keep the anchor-rate up to a capped step-up (max 8%/year) to reflect predictable scale.
- True-up and refunds: unused credits at contract milestones convert to account credits for future usage or are refundable per the schedule.

Benefits: predictable unit economics, partial upfront to secure capacity/priority, no full-year cash drain, and a mechanism for CloudNova to avoid surprise spikes.

I attached a short term sheet and a sample credit schedule. If this looks promising, we can map to a DocuSign and finance-friendly payment schedule (quarterly drawdown or two installments). Rishi — can you confirm if sales can extend a one-time onboarding credit to offset the initial deposit? Monica — I included finance to confirm escrow operationalization and refund rules.

Next steps: Amy — quick call tomorrow to walk the schedule? I can share a 1-page summary for your CFO.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Amy — quick update after internal alignment. We ran a tailored schedule for the 24-month anchor with a 30% phased deposit and the escrowed credit account. Key commercial terms we’d propose for CloudNova: 
- Term: 24 months
- Initial deposit: 20% due at signature, additional 10% due 30 days after signature (total 30% year-1 commit in escrow)
- Anchor unit rate: fixed for the 24-month period for hit-models listed in Annex A
- Usage ramp: if month-over-month usage exceeds the committed baseline by >25% in any rolling 90-day window, incremental usage billed at a pre-agreed overage rate (capped at +8% over anchor)
- Unused credits: annual true-up; refundable within 60 days of the anniversary, or converted to a credit with 12-month expiry if CloudNova opts in. Refunds processed to original payment method.
- Onboarding credit: Redwood will apply a one-time $25k onboarding credit against first invoice to reduce initial cash outlay.

I attached the updated term sheet (v2) and a sample amortization of the escrow credits across 24 months. If that addresses procurement concerns, we can prepare a DocuSign and include the escrow annex for legal review. Would you like a 30-min call Thursday to walk the commercial and the billing mock?

Best,
Laura Bennett
